name: alakazam_ml_v22
model: The v21 LightGBM ranker, features, confidence threshold, live ML scope, and 60-card deck are unchanged. v22 changes deterministic route control for Dudunsparce cycling, sufficient-hand stopping, Dunsparce cycle rebuilds, and explicit Fezandipiti ex alternate-attacker investment.
model_scope: Live ML remains restricted to safe Abra/Dunsparce bench-role choice and same-evolution-card target choice. Attack, Energy, Trainer, Boss, Hammer, retreat, abilities, END, KO promotion, effect-driven switching, continuity, and Fezandipiti route commitment remain deterministic.

source_evidence.interpretation: The three agents use the same 60 cards. The robust common signal is not maximum hand size but repeated attack availability, roughly three Dudunsparce cycles in wins, and a concrete next attacker. Majkel additionally converts Fezandipiti ex into a real alternate attack route.

v22_rule_changes: Treat only backup_eta <= 1 as a safe replacement attacker; a visible Abra or Kadabra alone no longer stops a continuity draw.
Use a soft 13-card sufficient-hand target: optional Dudunsparce, Hilda, Dawn, Poke Pad, and Enriching draws stop when current offense and a one-turn backup are secured.
Keep drawing above the target when the current KO is not the final win and backup_eta remains greater than one, subject to the existing deck floor.
Raise Dunsparce re-benching priority after the engine has cycled away and the current attacker lacks a deterministic replacement.

Allow progressive Fezandipiti ex Energy investment only for a visible <=100 HP/high-value target, effect-lock escape, or Rocket Articuno breaker route, and only after current Alakazam offense plus a one-turn backup are safe.
Recognize a powered Fezandipiti ex as an attack-ready KO promotion when Cruel Arrow can take a visible Bench prize.
Preserve exact-current-KO hand-spend protection, late two-prize exposure gates, deck floors, terminal wins, Boss logic, effect prevention, and the v21 ML boundary.

local_validation.illegal_selects: not measurable without official cg arena

diagnostic_controls.ALAKAZAM_V22_HAND_TARGET: 13 by default; soft target, not a hard cap
diagnostic_controls.ALAKAZAM_V22_CONTINUITY_DECK_BUFFER: 4 cards above the dynamic deck floor
diagnostic_controls.ALAKAZAM_V22_FEZ_PROGRESSIVE_BUILD: 1 by default; set 0 for v21-style one-Energy-short behavior

known_limitations: No official cg package or live arena was present in this environment, so Validation Episode, local self-play, and rating improvement are not proven.
The v22 Fezandipiti route is deterministic and requires visible public goals; it does not speculate about hidden future targets.
The model was intentionally not retrained because the current live ML scope does not control the decisions changed in v22.
Teacher-forced full replay comparison could not be rerun without the official observation deserializer; the new behavior is covered by self-contained golden-state tests instead.
